content.key_idea: 3D Gaussian Splatting renders a scene by projecting, sorting, and rasterizing Gaussians per tile, then backpropagating pixel loss; SLAM reuses this same per-frame rendering loop to alternately refine camera pose (tracking) and the Gaussian map (mapping).
content.reading_order: Top row (a) left to right through 5 numbered steps of 3DGS training; bottom row (b) two side-by-side sub-flows, tracking then mapping, each left to right.

summary: This background figure has two stacked panels. Panel (a) walks through one iteration of 3D Gaussian Splatting training in five numbered steps: projecting 3D Gaussians to 2D splats, sorting them per image tile into Gaussian tables, rendering pixel colors per tile, comparing against ground truth to get loss and gradients, and updating the Gaussians. Panel (b) shows how 3DGS-SLAM reuses this rendering loop twice per frame: a tracking sub-flow that holds Gaussians fixed and updates the camera pose from loss against the previous frame, and a mapping sub-flow that holds the pose fixed and updates the Gaussians. The figure uses flat/hatched colored boxes, small vector icons of a camera frame and Gaussian ellipsoids, and circled step numbers to guide reading order.
summary_zh: 该图为背景介绍图，分两部分：(a)以五个编号步骤展示3D高斯泼溅训练流程（投影、排序、渲染、计算损失与梯度、更新高斯）；(b)展示3DGS-SLAM如何复用该渲染流程分别完成位姿跟踪与建图两个子循环。
